title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of the HMG‐CoA Reductase Inhibitor Rosuvastatin and Natural Styryl Lactone Cryptomoscatone E1

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Racemic <jats:italic>syn</jats:italic>‐ethyl (<jats:italic>E</jats:italic>)‐2‐(2,2‐dimethyl‐6‐styryl‐1,3‐dioxan‐4‐yl)acetate is hydrolyzed with high enantioselectivity by Novozyme‐435 in 0.05 <jats:sc>m</jats:sc> sodium phosphate buffer at room temperature. The optically pure unreacted ethyl 2‐((4<jats:italic>R</jats:italic>,6<jats:italic>S</jats:italic>)‐2,2‐dimethyl‐6‐((<jats:italic>E</jats:italic>)‐styryl)‐1,3‐dioxan‐4‐yl)acetate and hydrolyzed (4<jats:italic>S</jats:italic>,6<jats:italic>R</jats:italic>)‐acid are used in the synthesis of HMG‐CoA reductase inhibitor rosuvastatin and the naturally occurring styryl lactone cryptomoscatone E1, respectively.</jats:p>
